arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Ms. Smith argued the Sixth Circuit exceeded its authority under appellate rules and Supreme Court precedent.
Mr. Shors argued the court of appeals corrected a clear error in its prior decision.
Justice Kennedy asked if the mandate issuance can be extended after certiorari denial.
Justice Souter asked if the court can extend or truncate the time for action.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case tests the limits of appellate court power. The core issue is whether a court of appeals retains authority to withdraw its mandate after the Supreme Court denies certiorari.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: the side that brought the case wants the Supreme Court to declare the Sixth Circuit's withdrawal of its mandate invalid.
the opposing side wants the Supreme Court to uphold the Sixth Circuit's power to withdraw its mandate.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case defines the finality of appellate judgments. It determines when a lower court can alter its decision after higher court review ends. The outcome affects the stability of legal proceedings and the authority of appellate courts.
